_comment: Allowlist for scripts/check_test_weakening.py (Layer 4, #52). Replaced the ALLOW_TEST_WEAKEN=1 environment override on 2026-08-08 — that was a blanket, invisible, whole-run bypass that silenced every file at once, left no trace in the reviewed diff, and was wired to a PR label in both CI workflows so it could be set from outside the repo. Each entry sanctions ONE file's deletion with an EXACT delta and a written reason. Governance mirrors .health-endpoint-allowlist.json / .urllib-httperror-close-allowlist.json: rationale >= 40 chars, malformed entries hard-fail. Two rules are specific to this guard: (1) an entry grants exactly its recorded allowed_delta — a measured delta WORSE than the entry fails, so an entry can never absorb future weakening of the same file; (2) a file with no entry fails as before. DO NOT widen an allowed_delta to make a new failure go away: that converts a one-time sanction into a permanent licence for the file, which is the hole this mechanism replaced.
_stale_policy: A STALE entry (file absent from the branch diff, or measured delta better than recorded) is a WARNING printed on every run, NOT a hard error — deliberately unlike the sibling allowlists, whose input is the filesystem. This guard diffs against merge-base(origin/master, HEAD), which MOVES: the moment a branch carrying an entry merges, its file leaves the diff and the entry goes stale through nobody's fault, and hard-failing would turn master red for everyone. The two ADR-0215 train entries this file used to carry (test_scope_filter_e2e.py, test_v5_42_2_branch_default_e2e.py) were removed on 2026-08-12 by 0047 C15a under exactly that instruction: the train had merged, both files were absent from BOTH merge-base 92dbb4b5 and HEAD, so neither could ever re-enter the branch diff and neither entry could ever stop warning. An entry whose staleness is unresolvable is noise that teaches the next reader to skim the warnings — delete it as this policy directs, and never widen an allowed_delta to silence one.
_entries: none — the allowlist is deliberately empty. Adding one sanctions deleting test coverage and is a decision for the owner, not a way past a red guard.
